title: metadata-admin designer keeps the retired form-view `visibleOn` as a live internal dialect: `anchors.ts` writes it on two view-create properties and `SchemaForm`'s `readVisibility` still reads `visibleWhen ?? visibleOn` over spec-served FormViews
body:
Filing gate ①: an out-of-scope finding (class b) from the os-dev report on objectui#12654 (comment `6216882809`, `carrier: none — seat to file`). Filed by the `domain:ui` seat 1 (`session_011K9g23W67dy2zwnyzaoB6o`). ⛔ Not a claim; for triage to grade and route.

reach: named producer, the designer itself. objectui#12654 (PR #12692) stops the console form page, plugin-form's `normalizeSectionField` and `SchemaRenderer` from reading the spec's retired form-view `visibleOn` / page-component `visibility`. The metadata-admin designer still writes and reads the old spelling, so after that PR it is the one reader left.

## Measured on objectui main `efa9cb4`

- **Writer.** `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/anchors.ts:282` and `:292` set `visibleOn: "data.viewKind == 'list'"` / `"data.viewKind == 'form'"` on the view anchor's create-schema properties (`kind`, `formType`). `view-create-body.test.ts:148-149` pins both. These are the only non-test `visibleOn:` writes in `packages/app-shell` and `apps/console`.
- **Reader.** `SchemaForm.tsx:1073-1076`, `readVisibility(node)`, returns `node?.visibleWhen ?? node?.visibleOn`. It has 5 call sites (`:1213`, `:1557`, `:1570`, `:1696`, `:3172`), covering top-level create-schema properties and FormView sections and fields. The FormViews come from both the app's own layouts and spec-served view metadata. The comment at `:1057-1069` names the in-app create schemas as the reason the fallback stays.
- **Type.** `form-spec.ts:219` / `:271` declare `FormSectionSpec.visibleOn` and `FormFieldSpec.visibleOn`. The `:131` comment says "One vocabulary per document", but the type carries both.
- **Stale prose.** Doc comments still call the predicate `visibleOn`: `predicate.ts:4`, `view-schema.ts:13`, `page-schema.ts:17`, `report-schema.ts:15`, `mergeServerFields.ts:23`, and the three inspectors (`PageDefaultInspector`, `ReportDefaultInspector`, `ViewVariantInspector`).
- **Not saved metadata.** The F4 measure on objectui#12654 (0 writes of `visibleOn` into saved metadata) still holds. The writes are in-app TypeScript layouts, not persisted rows.

## Why it is a defect, not a style point

The spec retired `visibleOn` on FormView (`retiredKey`, never). Under the declaration-is-enforcement rule, a reader that still folds the retired key in is consumer-side tolerance. A FormView an AI authors with `visibleOn` renders correctly in the designer's preview, yet is refused or ignored everywhere else. That is exactly the masked mistake the four axes rule out. The fix looks mechanical:
- re-spell the two `anchors.ts` writes as `visibleWhen`;
- update their pins;
- drop the `?? visibleOn` leg and the two `form-spec.ts` members;
- fix the prose.

One thing to measure first: `CONDITION_FIELD_NAMES` (`SchemaForm.tsx:956`) lists `visibleOn` as a property *name* that gets the condition widget. Whether any served schema still has a property literally named `visibleOn` decides whether that entry stays.

Dedupe: `search_issues` in objectui with "metadata-admin designer SchemaForm readVisibility visibleOn anchors view-create-body retired key" (16 results) and "visibleOn visibleWhen dialect form designer create schema" (27 results). The nearest are objectui#2212, #6111, #11630 and #11044, all closed. None covers the designer's own dialect.
